newsitem.title: FRANCE: VASARELY URGES CHIRAC TO SAVE BANKRUPT MUSEUM.
newsitem.headline: VASARELY URGES CHIRAC TO SAVE BANKRUPT MUSEUM.

text.p: The family of ailing artist Victor Vasarely, who designed the near-bankrupt Aix-en-Provence museum bearing his name in southern France, has urged President Jacques Chirac to help save the popular tourist spot from closure.

"Vasarely, this artist whom you admire, is going to die, confronted with waste and ingratitude," the 90-year-old's daughter-in-law Michele wrote in a letter published by the newspaper Le Figaro on Tuesday.

With the Hungarian-born Vasarely stricken with cancer, she accused public authorities of failing to prevent a financial debacle engulfing the Vasarely Foundation and threatening it with closure despite visits by hundred of thousands of tourists since 1976.

"Will we have to wait for an old man...to die, his heart and spirit torn apart by the blindness and ingratitude of France, for justice to be rendered to him? That will be too late," Michele Vasarely wrote.

In 1993, the Foundation was bailed out to the tune of a record 18.9 million francs ($3 million). A recent report by tax authorities reported the mysterious disappearance of hundreds of works, for a total value of 42 million francs ($8.4 million).
Vasarely was the champion of the 1960s "Op Art" movement, producing abstract geometrical works creating optical illusion of movement.
